metadata.title: Lil'Jordan Humphrey - Back on Denver's 53-man roster
metadata.description: The Broncos signed Humphrey off the practice squad to the active roster Friday.
metadata.analysis: It'll be Humphrey's third stint on the Broncos' 53-man roster this season, and it comes after the team placed Pat Bryant (ankle) on injured reserve. Humphrey's lone appearance in the regular season was in Week 2 against the Jaguars, when he failed to haul in his lone target while playing only three offensive snaps. He'll operate in a depth role at wide receiver behind Jaylen Waddle, Courtland Sutton, Troy Franklin and Marvin Mims.

metadata.title: Lil'Jordan Humphrey - Remaining in Denver organization
metadata.description: Humphrey signed a practice-squad contract with the Broncos on Saturday, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
metadata.analysis: Humphrey was released by Denver on Friday but quickly inked a deal to remain in the organization. However, Gabriel notes that the Broncos aren't elevating anyone for Sunday's matchup against San Francisco, so Humphrey won't be active while he resides on the practice squad. The veteran wideout has logged just three offensive snaps so far this season and didn't catch his only target.

metadata.title: Lil'Jordan Humphrey - Released by Denver
metadata.description: Humphrey was released by the Broncos on Friday, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
metadata.analysis: Fullback Adam Prentice was signed to the 53-man roster from the practice squad, so Humphrey was released in a corresponding move. However, assuming Humphrey wants to remain with the Broncos, there's a good chance the team will bring him back, even if it means he'll work as a member of the practice squad.

metadata.title: Lil'Jordan Humphrey - Back with Denver
metadata.description: The Broncos signed Humphrey on Tuesday, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Humphrey was released by the Broncos just hours before Monday's Week 1 loss to the Chiefs. The wide receiver was let go as a procedural move to manage the game-day roster limit and elevate players from the practice squad. Humphrey's return likely means the wide receiver will return to his role as a run blocker and occasionally targeted weapon for the Denver offense.

metadata.title: Lil'Jordan Humphrey signs with Broncos
metadata.description: The Broncos signed WR Lil'Jordan Humphrey to their active roster.
metadata.analysis: Humphrey will add depth in the wide receiver room for Denver.

metadata.title: Lil'Jordan Humphrey - Cut before season opener
metadata.description: The Broncos released Humphrey on Monday, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
metadata.analysis: Though he appeared to secure a roster spot coming out of the preseason as the Broncos' No. 6 receiver, Humphrey wound up being cut just hours before the team's season opener versus the Chiefs. Regarded as a strong blocking receiver who has been part of a mainstay on head coach Sean Payton's squads dating back to their time together in New Orleans, Humphrey is expected to eventually re-sign with Denver as a member of the roster or practice squad.

metadata.title: Lil'Jordan Humphrey - Re-ups with Broncos
metadata.description: Denver re-signed Humphrey on Thursday, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Humphrey kicked off the 2025 campaign wearing a Giants uniform, but he was poached off New York's practice squad by the Broncos in advance of a Week 11 game against Kansas City and provided the team with depth at wideout behind  Courtland Sutton, Troy Franklin, Pat Bryant and Marvin Mims down the stretch. Now, heading into his age-28 season, Humphrey appears positioned to reprise a similar reserve role.

metadata.title: Lil'Jordan Humphrey re-signs with Broncos
metadata.description: The Broncos re-signed WR Lil'Jordan Humphrey.
metadata.analysis: Humphrey returned for his second stint in Denver last season. He will remain in a depth role in the Broncos wide receiver room.

metadata.title: Broncos Re-Sign Lil'Jordan Humphrey
metadata.description: The Denver Broncos are re-signing wide receiver Lil'Jordan Humphrey to an undisclosed deal on Thursday, a source told Zac Stevens of DNVR Sports. Humphrey played three games with the New York Giants at the beginning of last year before the Broncos picked him up. Head coach Sean Payton is familiar with the 27-year-old wideout after he played the first three years of his career with the New Orleans Saints from 2019 through 2021. In his seven regular-season games with the Broncos in 2025, Humphrey caught nine of his 15 targets for 101 yards and one touchdown. He also played in Denver in 2023 and 2024, catching 44 of his 64 targets for 455 yards and four touchdowns in 34 games (15 starts). He will return to Denver to provide them with depth at the position, but he won't be anywhere near the fantasy radar behind Courtland Sutton, Troy Franklin, Pat Bryant, and Marvin Mims Jr.

metadata.title: Lil'Jordan Humphrey - Underwhelming season in 2025
metadata.description: Humphrey ended the 2025 regular season with 13 receptions on 25 targets for 156 yards and a touchdown across 10 regular season games.
metadata.analysis: Humphrey began the 2025 campaign with the Giants, recording four receptions for 55 yards over three games. The Broncos signed the veteran wideout away from New York's practice squad ahead of Denver's Week 11 matchup against the Chiefs. The veteran wideout rejoined the Broncos, having spent the previous two seasons in Denver. Humphrey provided depth in a familiar offense behind Courtland Sutton, Troy Franklin, Pat Bryant and Marvin Mims. The 27-year-old will become an unrestricted free agent this offseason, so he'll hope to be signed by a team looking for help in their wide receiver room ahead of the 2026 campaign. It's possible, however, that Humphrey could re-sign with the Broncos based on his familiarity with head coach Sean Payton's system.

metadata.title: Lil'Jordan Humphrey - Cashes in TD in postseason win
metadata.description: Humphrey brought in two of five targets for 33 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos' 33-30 overtime divisional-round win over the Bills on Saturday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran journeyman delivered with a 29-yard scoring grab just before halftime, his first touchdown since Week 15 and only his second since the start of a regular season he opened with the Giants. Humphrey is likely set for another modest complementary role in the upcoming AFC Championship Game matchup against either the Texans or Patriots, but he'll operate with Jarrett Stidham as his quarterback following Bo Nix's postseason-ending ankle fracture Saturday.

metadata.title: Lil'Jordan Humphrey - Finishes another quiet season
metadata.description: Humphrey ended the 2025 regular season with 13 receptions on 25 targets for 156 yards and a touchdown across 10 games.
metadata.analysis: After beginning the season with the Giants and recording just four grabs for 55 yards over three games, Humphrey was signed away from New York's practice squad by the Broncos ahead of the team's Week 11 matchup against the Chiefs. The veteran wideout was reunited with the Broncos after spending the previous two seasons in Denver. He joined a crowded wide receiver room, providing depth in a familiar offense behind Courtland Sutton, Troy Franklin, Pat Bryant and Marvin Mims. Humphrey will become an unrestricted free agent this offseason, so he'll hope to garner interest from teams around the league ahead of the 2026 campaign. With that said, it wouldn't be surprising to see the 27-year-old re-sign with the Broncos based on his familiarity with head coach Sean Payton's system, though he would have an uphill battle for meaningful playing time once again.

metadata.title: Lil'Jordan Humphrey - Catches two passes in win
metadata.description: Humphrey caught two of five targets for 23 yards in Denver's 20-13 win over Kansas City on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Humphrey's five targets were his most in a game since joining the Broncos on Nov. 12. With Pat Bryant (concussion) absent against the Chiefs, Humphrey operated as the Broncos' WR2 in terms of playing time, getting in on 60 percent of the offensive snaps, ahead of both Marvin Mims (47 percent) and Troy Franklin (38 percent). In six games with the Broncos, Humphrey has nine catches for 101 yards and one touchdown on 15 targets.
